QUOTE: The worker is detached (`external_bridge.cpp:1222`) and captures `this` and `handle_`. `stop()` (`:826`) does not wait for it. It joins the accept thread and the per-client threads only. So if the bridge is destroyed while an async ask is still running, the worker can use freed memory.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer identifies run_async_ask as the detached worker with no join in stop(), outliving the caller's scope. It also says every other spawn is joined, so it is the one detached thread.
